title: Go: Variables and Constants
description: Declare variables using var, :=, and const in Go.

steps.title: Declare with var
steps.description: Declare a variable `city` of type `string` with value `"Tokyo"` using the `var` keyword and print it.
hints: The type goes after the variable name in Go.

verification.failureMessage: Declare city with var and print it.

steps.title: Short Assignment :=
steps.description: Use the short assignment operator `:=` to declare `name := "Gopher"` and print it.
hints: `:=` declares and assigns in one step.
Type inference figures out the type for you.

verification.failureMessage: Use := to declare name and print it.

steps.title: Multiple Variables
steps.description: Declare multiple variables `x, y int = 10, 20` on one line and print their sum.
hints: `var x, y int = 10, 20` declares both on one line.
Print `x + y` or print each variable separately.

verification.failureMessage: Declare x=10, y=20 and print their sum 30.

steps.title: Constants with const
steps.description: Declare a constant `Greeting` with value `"Hello"` using `const` and print it.

verification.failureMessage: Use const to declare Greeting and print it.

steps.title: Zero Values
steps.description: Declare `var number int` and `var flag bool` without assigning values, then print both to see their zero values.
hints: In Go, declared variables without initial values get zero values.

verification.failureMessage: Print an uninitialized int and bool to see '0 false'.
